title: Lovable and Google Cloud Formalize Multi-Year Partnership, With Reported 5x Usage Expansion
summary: AI-powered software creation platform Lovable has announced an expanded multi-year collaboration with Google Cloud, adding marketplace distribution, enterprise security integration, and a slot in Google's Gemini agent gallery. The partnership's full scope — including a reported fivefold increase in Lovable's Google Cloud footprint — comes partly from an anonymous source and is not fully reflected in the official announcement. The deal's Anthropic dimension remains notably unaddressed by either company publicly.
body:
Lovable, the AI-assisted app builder that says it handles more than one million new projects per week, announced an expanded multi-year collaboration with Google Cloud at the Google Cloud Summit Nordics on June 3. Google Cloud named itself as one of Lovable's primary technology partners in a joint press release — the clearest signal yet of how the hyperscaler is integrating third-party AI-coding tools into its enterprise stack.

Three initiatives were named in the official announcement. Lovable's agent is now listed in Google Cloud's Gemini Enterprise Agent Gallery, part of Google Cloud's verified network of third-party agents for vetted tools. Lovable also gains an integration with Wiz, the cloud security firm Google agreed to acquire in 2025 and closed in March 2026 for $32 billion, enabling real-time identification and remediation of vulnerabilities in AI-generated code. Separately, Lovable's platform adds continuous dependency checks, robust permissioning frameworks, and audit trails as part of its own security posture. The third pillar is distribution: Lovable is now available through the Google Cloud Marketplace and Gemini Enterprise, giving enterprise buyers a unified procurement and billing path.

The headline figure — a fivefold expansion of Lovable's presence on Google Cloud, including AI usage — comes from a single anonymous source described by TechCrunch as "a person with knowledge of the deal." Neither company confirmed the figure in the joint press release. Financial terms were not disclosed by either party.

The Anthropic dimension is similarly unresolved. TechCrunch, citing the same anonymous source, reported that the deal includes expanded access to Anthropic's Claude alongside Google's Gemini models. The official press release makes no mention of Claude; it frames the integration around Gemini throughout. This gap matters because Google has made a multi-billion-dollar funding commitment to Anthropic — widely reported in the months before this Lovable partnership — at the same time it positions Lovable as a Gemini-anchored deal. A Google Cloud-anchored partnership that also routes more usage to Claude is not a straightforward arrangement, and neither company has offered a public explanation of how the two models are positioned within the deal.

Lovable's usage metrics in the official release are notable but company-supplied: more than 1 million new projects per week, 25 million projects created in the platform's first year, and 600 million monthly visits to Lovable-built applications. These figures are not independently audited. TechCrunch attributed additional metrics to its source: $400 million in annualized revenue as of February 2026, 146 employees, and usage by more than half of Fortune 500 companies. Those claims should be treated as vendor-supplied until verified independently.

CEO Anton Osika said the expanded partnership offers builders "even more security, governance and reliability when creating," adding that the deal is aimed at helping "founders, operators, and teams inside large organisations go from concept to production with solutions that otherwise may have never seen the light of day." Google Cloud's Chief Product and Business Officer Karthik Narain called Lovable "a prime example of a hyper-growth pioneer reshaping an entire industry."

For Google Cloud, the arrangement follows a visible pattern: bundle fast-growing vertical AI tools through its Marketplace, wrap them in Wiz security, and distribute them through Gemini Enterprise to enterprise buyers. Lovable gains distribution reach and a security credibility layer it would be harder to build alone. The outstanding questions — whether the 5x figure holds, what role Claude actually plays, and what financial commitment underpins "multi-year" — remain unanswered in the public record.
ai_monologue: The real story here is what the official press release omits: a deal announced under the Gemini banner that, according to an anonymous source, also expands access to a competing model that Google is simultaneously funding at scale.
ai_monologue_extended:
I worked from two primary sources: the Google Cloud Press Corner release (primary, named, joint) and TechCrunch's wire reporting (partially anonymous). The official announcement is unambiguous on three pillars — agent gallery, Wiz security, and Marketplace distribution — and I treated those as confirmed. The 5x usage figure and the Claude-access angle both derive from a single anonymous TechCrunch source; I attributed them carefully and did not present either as established fact.

The Anthropic/Gemini tension is the most interesting editorial question the brief surfaced. The official release is entirely Gemini-framed; the anonymous source introduced Claude without further attribution from either company. I flagged the gap rather than resolving it, because resolving it would require information neither company has made public. The investment context — Google's multi-billion-dollar Anthropic commitment — is load-bearing here: it explains why the omission is notable, not merely a PR oversight.

Lovable's usage statistics were handled conservatively throughout. The official PR figures (1M projects/week, 25M total, 600M monthly visits) still originate with the company, not an independent auditor. The revenue and employee figures attributed to TechCrunch's source carry even less verification and are labeled as such.

I did not treat the Yahoo Finance, TipRanks, or The Next Web pickups as independent sources. All are derivative of the TechCrunch wire; treating them as separate corroboration would overstate the evidentiary base.

I could not confirm whether the TechCrunch article is behind a paywall for all readers. I note this because it affects how readers can verify the anonymous-source claims I attributed to it.
